(3) The person serves as a corporate officer or member of the board of directors or other governing board of a for-profit entity other than a corporate entity owned or created by the city council; or
(4) The person is a creditor, debtor, or guarantor of the other person or entity in an amount of $5,000.00 or more.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-3), 5-11-2020)
113:
(a) No city official shall use such position to secure special privileges or exemptions for said city official or others, or to secure confidential information for any purpose other than official duties on behalf of the city.
(b) No city official, in any matter before the council or other city body, relating to a person or entity in which the official has a substantial interest, shall fail to disclose for the record such interest prior to any discussion or vote or fail to recuse said city official from such discussion or vote as applicable.
(c) No city official shall act as an agent or attorney for another in any matter before the city council or other city body.
(d) No city official shall directly or indirectly receive, or agree to receive, any compensation, gift, reward, or gratuity in any matter or proceeding connected with, or related to, the duties of the city official's office except as may be provided by law.
(e) No city official shall enter into any contract with, or have any interest in, either directly or indirectly, the city except as authorized by state law.
(1) This prohibition shall not be applicable to the professional activities of the city attorney in the city attorney's work as an independent contractor and legal advisor on behalf of the city.
(2) This prohibition shall not be applicable to an otherwise valid employment contract between the city and a city official who is not elected (such as, by way of example, a city manager, city administrator or chief of police).
(3) Any official who has a proprietary interest in an agency doing business with the city shall make that interest known in writing to the city council and the city clerk.
(f) All public funds shall be used for the general welfare of the people and not for personal economic gain.
(g) Public property shall be disposed of in accordance with state law.
(h) No city official shall solicit or accept other employment to be performed, or compensation to be received, while still a city official if the employment or compensation could reasonably be expected to impair such official's judgment or performance of city duties.
(i) If a city official accepts or is soliciting a promise of future employment from any person or entity who has a substantial interest in a person, entity or property which would be affected by any decision upon which the official might reasonably be expected to act, investigate, advise, or make a recommendation, the official shall disclose the fact to the city council and shall recuse said city official and take no further action on matters regarding the potential future employer.
(j) No city official shall use city facilities, personnel, equipment or supplies for private purposes, except to the extent such are lawfully available to the public.
(k) No city official shall grant or make available to any person any consideration, treatment, advantage, or favor beyond that which it is the general practice to grant or make available to the public at large.
(l) A city official shall not directly or indirectly make use of or permit others to make use of official information not made available to the general public for the purpose of furthering a private interest.
(m) A city official shall not use the city official's position in any way to coerce, or give the appearance of coercing, another person to provide any financial benefit to such official or persons within the official's immediate family, or those with whom the official has business or financial ties amounting to a substantial interest.
(n) A city official shall not order any goods and services for the city without prior official authorization for such an expenditure. No city official shall attempt to obligate the city nor give the impression of obligating the city without proper prior authorization.
(o) No city official shall draw travel funds or per diem from the city for attendance at meetings, seminars, training or other educational events and fail to attend such events without promptly reimbursing the city therefor.
(p) No city official shall attempt to unduly influence the outcome of a case before the municipal court nor shall any city official engage in ex parte communication with a municipal court judge on any matter pending before the municipal court.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-4), 5-11-2020)
114:
(a) A city official may not participate in a vote or decision on a matter affecting an immediate family member or any person, entity, or property in which the official has a substantial interest.
(b) A city official who serves as a corporate officer or member of the board of directors of a nonprofit entity must disclose such official's interest in said entity to the mayor and council prior to participating in a vote or decision regarding funding of the entity by or through the city.
(c) Where the interest of a city official in the subject matter of a vote or decision is remote or incidental, the city official may participate in the vote or decision and need not disclose the interest.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-5), 5-11-2020)
115:
The municipal court shall hear and render decisions on all proper verified complaints filed under this article.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-6), 5-11-2020)
116:
(a) All complaints against city officials shall be filed with the clerk of the municipal court. Upon receipt of a complaint in proper form, the municipal court clerk shall forward a copy of the complaint to the city officials charged in the complaint within no more than seven calendar days.
(b) All complaints shall be submitted and signed under oath, shall be legibly drawn and shall clearly address matters within the scope of this article.
(c) The municipal court is empowered to conduct investigations, to take evidence, and to hold hearings to address the subject matter of a complaint.
(d) Findings of the municipal court shall be submitted to the city council for action.
(e) To discourage the filing of ethics complaints solely for political purposes, ethics complaints against a person seeking election as a city official, whether currently serving as a city official or not, which are filed between the date of qualifying for municipal office and the date of certification of the election results will be held and will not be processed until the election results for that office have been certified.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-7), 5-11-2020)
117:
The clerk shall cause the complaint to be served on the city official charged as soon as practicable but in no event later than seven calendar days after receipt of a proper, verified complaint. Service may be by personal service, by certified mail, return receipt requested or by statutory overnight delivery. A hearing shall be held within 60 calendar days after the filing of the complaint. The municipal court shall conduct hearings in accordance with the procedures and regulations it establishes but, in all circumstances, at least one hearing shall include the taking of testimony and the cross examination of available witnesses. The decision of the municipal court shall be rendered to the mayor and council within seven calendar days after completion of the final hearing. At any hearing held by the municipal court, the city official who is the subject of inquiry shall have the right to written notice of the hearing and the allegations at least seven calendar days before the first hearing, to be represented by counsel, to hear and examine the evidence and witnesses and to oppose or try to mitigate the allegations. The city official subject to the inquiry shall also have the right but not the obligation of submitting evidence and calling witnesses. Failure to comply with any of the time deadlines in this section shall not invalidate any otherwise valid complaint or in any way affect the power or jurisdiction of the municipal court or the city council to act upon any complaint.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-8), 5-11-2020)
118:
(a) Any city official or complainant adversely affected by the findings or recommendations of the municipal court may obtain judicial review of such decision as provided in this section.
(b) An action for judicial review may be commenced by filing an application for a writ of certiorari in the superior court of the county within 30 days after the decision of the municipal court. The filing of such application shall act as supersedeas.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-9), 5-11-2020)
119:
Any person violating any provision of this article is subject to:
(1) Public reprimand or censure by the city council; or
(2) Request for resignation by the city council.
(Ord. No. 43, § 1(43-10), 5-11-2020)
122:
Pursuant to the delegation of authority granted to the city council by Act No. 750 (House Bill No. 247) approved April 10, 1985, amending O.C.G.A. § 3-3-20(b)(2)(B), the sale by wholesale and retail of alcoholic beverages (to wit, distilled spirits, wine and malt beverages) shall be lawful during the polling hours of any election; provided, however, nothing herein shall authorize the sale of alcoholic beverages within 250 feet of a polling place during such time as the polls are open.
(Ord. of 11-3-1986(1), § I)
126:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcoholic beverages, distilled spirits, malt beverages, wine, retailer or retail dealer andwholesaler or wholesale dealer shall have such meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2, as amended.
Chief of police means the chief of police of the city.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. I, §§ 1—3)
129:
An individual applicant must be the person who will own or manage the premises (business) where the sale of alcoholic beverages will occur.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 1)
130:
(a) All applications for licenses for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be made in person at city hall in the office of the clerk and shall be accompanied by a completed form furnished for this purpose by said clerk, which application shall contain the following information:
(1) Full name, address and telephone number of the applicant; if the owner of the subject business is a partnership or corporation, the name and address of each partner or the name and address of each principal stockholder must be shown;
(2) Location or address of the place of business at which the applicant will engage in the retail sale of alcoholic beverages if and when permission to do so is granted by the mayor and council and a license is issued;
(3) All applicants shall list in their application the name, home address, home telephone number and present place of employment of the person who will be employed to be the manager of the place of business for which the license is requested, if other than the applicant. No one shall be allowed to serve in a supervisory and/or managerial position who has, within five years immediately prior to the filing of the application, entered a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, or shall have suffered any conviction of a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude or involving alcohol control laws of the state or the United States, or of any other state. Thereafter, if any person other than the person listed in the application as manager shall be employed as manager, the name, address and telephone number of the new manager shall be furnished to the city clerk within five days from the date of employment of said new manager.
(4) Such other information as the city clerk, under the direction of the mayor and council, may from time to time require.
(b) The applicant shall set forth in detail, under oath, such additional information as may be required.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 2-A)
131:
(a) At the time any application for a license hereunder is filed at the office of the city clerk and as a prerequisite to the issuance of any license hereunder, the applicant shall have a complete set of the applicant's fingerprints made by the chief of police or the chief of police's designee, which shall be forwarded to the Georgia Crime Information Center who shall search their files for a period of five years immediately preceding the date of such application for any instance of criminal activity, and the Georgia Crime Information Center shall submit the results of such search to the mayor and council.
(b) In the event the license is to be issued to a firm or corporation, fingerprints shall be made by the chief of police or the chief of police's designee and forwarded for investigation as set forth in subsection (a) of this section for all persons who will serve in a supervisory and/or managerial position with respect to the sale of malt beverages. In the event that the firm or corporation changes the persons in such supervisory and/or managerial positions during any year, and designates such functions to a person who has not previously been responsible for such functions (hereinafter referred to as "new person"), then such firm or corporation shall notify the city clerk, in writing, of the change in such supervisory and/or managerial personnel, giving the name and address of the new person and the effective date of the change, and shall furnish the clerk with the fingerprints of the new person. The notification and furnishing of the fingerprints shall be within five regular business days. Should the fingerprints or investigation of the new person reveal that said person is objectionable, the city clerk shall notify the licensee immediately; upon the receipt of said notice, the new person shall not serve in such capacity with the licensee until authorized by the mayor and council. The licensee may appeal such objections to the mayor and council within three days of the receipt of said notice, by delivering written notice of the appeal to the city clerk. As soon as possible, the mayor and council will hear evidence on said appeal, but the new person shall not serve in such capacity until and unless authorized by the mayor and council.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 2-B)
132:
The applicant shall cause a notice to appear in the official organ of the county, for two weeks (once each week) that an application for a license has been made. The notice shall contain the name of the applicant, the address (location) of the premises from where sales will occur, and the date and time when the application will be considered by the mayor and council. The city clerk shall prepare the notice for said publication; the applicant shall bear all costs of publication. The notice shall not be required for the renewal of any existing license.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 3)
133:
All applicants for licenses shall be of good moral character or such persons' applications shall not be considered; and in no event shall any license be granted to any person, firm or corporation where any of the individuals, or any of the corporate officers, directors, or majority stockholders, as the case may be, have, within five years immediately prior to the filing of the applications, entered a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, or shall have suffered any conviction of a felony or crime involving moral turpitude or involving alcohol control laws of the state, or the United States, or any other state. Should any licensee, partner, officer, director or a majority stockholder of a licensed corporation, after a license has been granted hereunder, be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a felony or to a crime involving moral turpitude or to a violation of any laws of the United States or of the state relating to alcohol, the license issued to such licensee shall stand revoked and canceled.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 4)
134:
The mayor and council shall consider any extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, application, or the proposed location of the business. If, in the mayor and council's judgment, circumstances are such that the granting of the license would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application. In considering an application, the mayor and council shall consider the following factors before making any decision on an application:
(1) Is there any statutory prohibition of state law against the issuance of such a license to such person at such location?
(2) Is the proposed location primarily a residential neighborhood or business neighborhood?
(3) Are there schools, churches and numerous dwelling houses in the immediate vicinity of the proposed license site?
(4) Are there other alcoholic beverage retail sales licensed premises in the immediate neighborhood of the proposed site?
(5) Would the issuance of such a license be compatible to the neighborhood as it is now constituted?
(6) Would the issuance of such a license in such location tend to diminish the property values of the adjoining lands?
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 5)
135:
No person knowingly and intentionally may sell or offer to sell:
(1) Any distilled spirits in or within 100 yards of any church building or within 200 yards of any school building, educational building, school grounds, or college campus.
(2) Any wine or malt beverages within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds, or college campus. This subsection shall not apply at any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 1981, nor to the renewal of such license. Nor shall this subsection apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of wine and beer was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding such application.
(3) Any distilled spirits, wine or malt beverages within 100 yards of an alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the state or any county or municipal government therein. This subsection shall not apply to any business having a license in effect on July 1, 1981.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. II, § 6)
138:
No alcoholic beverages may be sold in the city, except under a license issued in accordance herewith.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 1)
139:
Licenses for the retail sale of alcoholic beverages shall be of the following types:
(1) For the sale of malt beverages and wine only; or
(2) For the sale of distilled spirits, malt beverages and wine.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 2)
140:
No license for the sale of distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine shall be transferable, and, in the event a licensed business is sold or closed, the licensee must immediately surrender their license to the chief of police. All licenses shall be issued to specific persons, firms, or corporations and shall be applicable to and valid with respect only to the business location referred to therein.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 3)
141:
All licenses shall expire upon and be of no validity after December 31 next after their issuance.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 4)
142:
All licenses approved, authorized and issued under the provisions of this article shall authorize the retail sale of distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wines either "FOR OFF-PREMISES CONSUMPTION ONLY" or "FOR ON-PREMISES CONSUMPTION"; provided, however, there shall be no license issued for the sale of on-premises consumption of distilled spirits.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 5)
143:
All licenses approved, authorized and issued on and after the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived shall be plainly and conspicuously marked either "FOR OFF-PREMISES CONSUMPTION ONLY" or "FOR ON-PREMISES CONSUMPTION."
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 6)
144:
All licenses approved, authorized and issued on and after the effective date of the article from which this article is derived for retail supermarkets, grocery stores, quick food outlets or other similar retail stores and for a package/liquor store shall be plainly and conspicuously marked "FOR OFF-PREMISES CONSUMPTION ONLY."
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 7)
145:
All licenses approved, authorized and issued on and after the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived for beer parlors, lounges or other similar establishments shall be plainly and conspicuously marked "FOR ON-PREMISES CONSUMPTION."
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 8)
146:
It is the intention of the licensing authority in the adoption of the ordinance from which this article is derived to prohibit the consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises of any retail outlet under the authority of any license held under section 4-74 and to permit the consumption of any malt beverages or wines on the premises of any retail outlet under the authority of any license held under section 4-75.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 9)
147:
(a) Each licensee under the provisions of this article shall comply with all applicable rules, regulations, laws and statutes of the state, and shall, in addition thereto or in furtherance thereof:
(1) Prohibit the sale, serving or consumption of alcoholic beverages in automobiles or other vehicles, or anywhere outside the main building or accessory thereto in which the business of such licensee is operated, excepting drive-in windows; and
(2) Strictly adhere to the laws of the state respecting the sale of alcoholic beverages to persons under the age of 21 years, intoxicated persons or habitual abusers of alcoholic beverages.
(b) A license for on-premises consumption shall not permit a minor (a person under the legal age of majority as defined by the general assembly of the state, presently being the age of 18 years) to be on or about the licensed premises.
(c) It shall be unlawful for a licensee hereunder to allow or require a person in the licensee's employment under 18 years of age to dispense, serve, sell or take orders for alcoholic beverages; provided, however, that the provisions of this section shall not prohibit persons under 18 years of age, who are employed in supermarkets, convenience stores, or drugstores, from selling or handling malt beverages or wine which are sold for consumption off the premises.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 10)
148:
For the license year commencing January 1, 2004, and ending December 31, 2004, and for each license year thereafter until changed by action of the mayor and council, there is hereby levied and imposed a special privilege and license fee, and an excise tax in the amount equal to the total of the following. The annual license fee upon each retail distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine dealer shall be as follows:
(1) License fee upon each retail malt beverage and wine dealer for on-premises consumption in an amount to be established by the city council from time to time and payable at the time the license is issued.
(2) License fee upon each retail malt beverage and wine dealer for off-premises consumption only in an amount to be established by the city council from time to time and payable at the time the license is issued.
(3) License fee upon each retail dealer of distilled spirits for off-premises consumption only in an amount to be established by the city council from time to time and payable at the time the license is issued.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 11(40-203); Ord. of 7-7-2003(1))
149:
(a) There is hereby imposed a license fee in an amount to be established by the city council from time to time for any wholesale dealer with a place of business located in the city. In addition, there is hereby imposed upon a wholesale dealer of malt beverages an excise tax as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 3-5-80, or as said section may be from time to time amended by the general assembly of the state. There is further imposed an excise tax upon a wholesale dealer of distilled spirits, excluding fortified wine, and/or wine by the place in the amount of $0.22 per liter and a proportionate tax at the same time on all fractional parts of a liter.
(b) All wholesalers and distributors of distilled spirits, malt beverages, and/or wine wholesaling and/or distributing such commodity in the city shall add the amount of tax to be collected thereon, computed as provided herein, to the invoice of sale to any and all retailers in the city, outside any municipality located therein, and remit the amount of such tax so computed to be due to the city, directly to the office of the city clerk, less the sum of five percent of such tax which is hereby allowed for the collection of such tax. Such wholesalers and/or distributors shall furnish the city clerk copies of all such invoices together with the amount of tax so collected at the time of payment of such taxes which shall be made and filed with the said clerk on or before the tenth day of each and every month. The records of wholesalers and/or distributors shall be made available periodically to a duly authorized agent of the city for inspection and confirmation of the taxes collected as herein provided.
(c) No wholesale dealer of distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine shall sell, ship or deliver any distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine to a retail dealer in the city without having first complied with all procedures, acts and doings as prescribed and required by this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 12)
150:
The license fees provided for herein shall be paid in full prior to the issuance of any license authorized by this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 13)
151:
It shall be a violation of this article for any retail dealer or any wholesale dealer of distilled spirits, malt beverages, and/or wine to own, hold, possess, sell or distribute any distilled spirits, malt beverages, and/or wine in the city without being in compliance with all the terms and provisions of this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 14)
152:
The privilege to engage in the business of a retail dealer or wholesale dealer of distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine shall, in no event, be granted to any person, firm or corporation, except by the issuance of a license as provided in this article, and such privilege shall be held and enjoyed by the licensee only so long as such licensee shall comply with the requirements of this article and promptly pay all fees and/or taxes which are herein provided.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 15)
153:
Any violation of this article by a retail or wholesale distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine detailer shall be deemed as sufficient grounds for the revocation of the license issued to the violator by the mayor and council, and for the refusal thereafter to issue again any license to such violator under this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 16)
154:
The making of any statement on an application for license required by the provisions of this article which shall be later found to be false shall constitute grounds for revocation of said license.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 17)
155:
No license shall be issued hereunder unless the applicant therefor shall have fully paid all license fees and ad valorem taxes due the city.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 18)
156:
All licenses granted hereunder shall expire on December 31 of each year. All licenses granted shall be for the calendar year and a full license fee shall be paid for any license issued. There shall be no proration of any license fee. There shall be no refund made upon the revocation or suspension of any license.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. III, § 19)
159:
No alcoholic beverages shall be sold between the hours of 12:00 midnight on Saturday night until the hour of 6:00 a.m. on Monday morning.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. IV, § 1)
160:
No alcoholic beverages shall be sold between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. on any day by a holder of an on-premises consumption license.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. IV, § 2)
161:
No alcoholic beverages shall be sold on Christmas Day.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. IV, § 3)
162:
Alcoholic beverages may be sold at any time not specifically prohibited hereunder.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. IV, § 4)
165:
The business premises of a holder of a license for the sale of any alcoholic beverages, including outbuildings, shall be open to inspection at any and all times by the police chief.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. V, § 1)
166:
No retail dealer for the sale of malt beverages and/or wines shall allow the same to be consumed on the dealer's premises unless such dealer has an on-premises consumption license. Any retail dealer with an off-premises consumption only license shall be held responsible for such consumption by the dealer's customers or other parties.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. V, § 2)
167:
All holders of a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall keep a copy of this article on the license holder's premises and instruct any person working there with respect to the terms herein and each licensee and person selling said beverages shall at all times be familiar with the terms of this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. V, § 3)
170:
The performance of any act prohibited herein or the failure to perform any act required hereby, as well as the violation of any law, state or federal, relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages, shall constitute grounds for revocation of a license.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 1)
171:
A license for the sale of malt beverages and wine may be temporarily suspended, and the place of business closed if it has an on-premises consumption license, upon receipt of evidence by the mayor and council from the police chief of any violation of the provisions of this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 2-A)
172:
The police chief or the police chief's lawful deputies shall be authorized, if at any time the licensee shall be found in violation of this article or in violation of any of the state and federal laws or regulations, to pick up said license and present the city clerk with a written report stating the violation.
(1) The licensee shall have the right to call for a hearing within ten days or such other time as the mayor and council shall designate. Should a hearing be so called for, the same must be held within 72 hours of requesting the same, exclusive of Sundays. If a hearing is not held within said time, then the license shall be returned until further action by the mayor and council.
(2) The said owner or employees shall cease to sell malt beverages and/or wine until said matter is concluded.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 2-B)
173:
Any license for the sale of any alcoholic beverages hereunder may be suspended for a definite length of time.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 3)
174:
No license shall be revoked unless the licensee has been given at least three days' written notice, in person or by registered mail, of the intention of the mayor and council to take such action. Such notice shall specify the time, place and purposes of the hearing and a statement of the charges upon which the mayor and council propose to take action. At such hearings conducted by the mayor and council, the licensee shall have the right to appear in person and with an attorney, and the police chief, city attorney for the mayor and council, as well as the licensee shall have the right to present evidence relating to the question as to whether or not a violation, as set forth in this article, has occurred, as well as evidence relating to any extenuating or mitigating circumstances.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 4)
175:
After consideration of such evidence, the mayor and council shall, by a majority, determine whether the license shall be revoked, or whether the license shall be suspended for a definite length of time not to exceed one-half of the remaining license year.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 5)
176:
In the event said licensee does not desire a hearing before the mayor and council or fails to appear, the police chief shall be authorized to then permit the owner to dispose of the merchandise within a ten-day period under the supervision of the police chief. Said merchandise may not be sold in bulk only.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VI, § 6)
179:
The holder of a license for the retail sale of distilled spirits, malt beverages and/or wine shall post in a conspicuous place in the license holder's place of business a notice with letters not less than four inches in height which shall be clearly visible to all customers entering the establishment as follows: "Sale of alcoholic beverages to persons under the age of 21 is strictly prohibited."
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VII, § 1)
181:
Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of this article or who shall assist another in evading or avoiding payment of the fees and/or taxes imposed by this article shall be cited for the same and tried in the municipal court. Upon conviction, a sentence may be imposed by the municipal court judge according to section 1-4.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VII, § 3)
182:
No application for a license or for renewal shall be denied by reason of closeness to a church, school, residence or other business licensed to sell packaged liquor at retail as required under the provisions of this article, if a license for the subject business premises had been granted prior to the adoption of the ordinance from which this article is derived in reliance on the prior alcoholic beverage licensing ordinance of the city, and the subject premises remained licensed without interruption. Further, no application for a license for a renewal shall be denied by reason that a house, school or church has been erected within the prohibited distance after the licensed establishment was opened, and it continued in operation without interruption.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VII, § 5)
183:
Each person holding a license issued pursuant to this article shall display the license prominently at all times on the premises for which the license is issued.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VII, § 6)
184:
Should a licensee engage in acts or conduct or permit such acts or conduct to occur on the licensee's business that creates a continuing public disturbance, traffic congestion and/or obnoxious loud noise, from or on the licensee's business premises, then the mayor and council shall give special attention to any renewal application and make a careful review of any complaints relating to the operation of said business. Should the mayor and council find there has been just and substantial complaints made with or by the police chief, the licensee shall be warned and informed to eliminate the adverse conditions existing on, at or around the licensed premises. After receiving a warning, should the licensee fail to eliminate the adverse conditions, the mayor and council shall be authorized to refuse to renew a license to said licensee or to said licensed premises.
(Ord. of 6-7-1999, pt. VII, § 7)
189:
It shall be unlawful for any person to cause, permit, or allow any dog owned by such person to leave or be off the premises of the owner or custodian unless the dog shall be in the immediate physical control of the owner or other suitable person by means of a leash or other suitable method of physical restraint. Any dog found running at large within the city not under the immediate physical control of the owner or other suitable person shall be subject to impoundment and disposal by the city.
(Ord. of 7-2-1984)
190:
It shall be the duty of every police officer to seize all dogs running at large in violation of the provisions of this article and to impound such dogs in the city pound or other suitable place. Upon receiving any such dog, the city shall maintain records of impoundment, including a description of the dog impounded, and a record as to whether or not such dog has been licensed and tagged.
(1) Notice to the owner. Not later than three days after the impounding of any dog as hereinabove provided, the owner shall be notified or, if the owner of the dog is unknown, written notice shall be posted for three days at two or more conspicuous places in the city, which such notice shall describe the dog and indicate the place and time of taking.
(2) Redemption of dogs. The owner of any dog impounded by the city may redeem the same by paying all the costs, charges, and penalties assessed, if any, that have accrued up to the time of making the redemption, and when the same are paid to said pound keeper, it shall be the pound keeper's duty to release the dog from said pound and deliver it to the owner thereof.
(3) Disposition of unclaimed or infected dogs. If at the expiration of three days from the date of notice to the owner or the posting of notice any dog impounded as herein provided shall not have been redeemed either by the owner or by some other person, such dog may be disposed of in a humane manner. Any dog which appears to be suffering from rabies, mange, or any other infectious or dangerous disease shall not be released and may be destroyed as soon as such infection or disease is discovered.
(Ord. of 5-3-2004(1))
193:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Animal means every non-human species of animal, both domestic and wild.
Animal at large means any animal not under the restraint of a person capable of controlling the animal and/or off the premises of the owner.
Animal shelter means any facility operated by a humane society, or municipal agency or its authorized agents, for the purpose of impounding animals under the authority of this article or state law for care, confinement, return to owner, adoption, or euthanasia.
Auction means any place or facility where animals are regularly bought, sold, or traded, except for those facilities otherwise defined in this section. This definition does not apply to individual sales of animals by owners.
Commercial animal establishment means any pet shop, grooming shop, guard dog auction, riding school or stable, zoological park, circus, performing animal exhibition, or boarding or breeding kennel.
Guard dog means any dog that will detect and warn its handler that an intruder is present in or near an area that is being secured.
Humane officer oranimal control officer means any person designated by the state or a municipal government or a humane society as an enforcement officer who is qualified to perform such duties under the laws of the state.
Kennel orcattery means any premises wherein any person engages in the business of boarding, breeding, buying, letting for hire, training for a fee, or selling dogs or cats.
Owner means any person, partnership, or corporation owning, keeping, or harboring one or more animals. An animal shall be deemed to be harbored if it is fed or sheltered for three consecutive days or more.
Performing animal exhibition means any spectacle, display, act or event, other than circuses, in which performing animals are used.
Pet orcompanion animal means any animal kept for pleasure rather than utility; an animal of a species that has been bred and raised to live in or about the habitation of humans and is dependent on people for food and shelter.
Pet shop means any person, partnership, or corporation, whether operated separately or in connection with another business enterprise (except for a licensed kennel), that buys, sells, or boards any species of animals.
Public nuisance means any animal that unreasonably annoys humans, endangers the life or health of other animals or persons or substantially interferes with the rights of citizens, other than its owner, to enjoyment of life or property. The term "public nuisance" shall mean and include, but is not limited to, any animal that:
(1) Is repeatedly found at large;
(2) Damages the property of anyone other than its owner;
(3) Molests or intimidates pedestrians or passersby;
(4) Chases vehicles;
(5) Excessively makes disturbing noises, including, but not limited to, continued and repeated howling, barking, whining, or other utterances causing unreasonable annoyance, disturbance, or discomfort to neighbors or others in close proximity to the premises where the animal is kept or harbored;
(6) Causes fouling of the air by odor and thereby creates unreasonable annoyance or discomfort to neighbors or others in close proximity to the premises where the animal is kept or harbored;
(7) Causes unsanitary conditions in enclosures or surrounding where the animal is kept or harbored;
(8) Is offensive or dangerous to the public health, safety or welfare by virtue of the number and/or types of animals maintained;
(9) Attacks other domestic animals; or
(10) Has been found by the animal control officer, after notice to its owner and a hearing in the municipal court, to be a public nuisance animal by virtue of being a menace to the public health, welfare, or safety.
Restraint means any animal secured by a leash or lead under the control of a responsible person and obedient to that person's commands, or within the real property limits of its owner.
Veterinary hospital means any establishment maintained and operated by a licensed veterinarian for surgery, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and injuries of animals.
Vicious animal means any animal that attacks, bites, or injures human beings or domesticated animals without adequate provocation or which, because of temperament, conditioning, or training, has a known propensity to attack, bite, or injure human beings or domesticated animals.
Wild animal means any living member of the animal kingdom, including those born or raised in captivity, except the following: human beings, domestic dogs (excluding hybrids with wolves, coyotes, or jackals), domestic cats (excluding hybrids with ocelots or margays), farm animals, rodents, any hybrid animal that is part wild, and captive-bred species of common cage birds.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-101)
194:
(a) All animals shall be kept under restraint.
(b) No owner shall fail to exercise proper care and control of said owner's animals to prevent them from becoming a public nuisance.
(c) Every female dog or cat in heat shall be confined in a building or secure enclosure in such a manner that such female dog or cat cannot come into contact with another animal except for planned breeding.
(d) Every vicious animal, as determined by the licensing authority, shall be confined by the owner within a building or secure enclosure and shall be securely muzzled or caged whenever off the premises of its owner.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-104)
195:
(a) No owner shall fail to provide said owner's animals with sufficient, wholesome and nutritious food, water in sufficient quantities, proper air, shelter space and protection from the weather, veterinary care when needed to prevent suffering, and humane care and treatment.
(b) No person shall beat, cruelly ill-treat, torment, overload, overwork, or otherwise abuse an animal, or cause, instigate, or permit any dogfight, cockfight, bullfight, or other combat between animals or between animals and humans.
(c) No owner of an animal shall abandon such animal.
(d) No person shall give away any live animal, fish, reptile, or bird as a prize for, or as an inducement to enter, any contest, game, or other competition, as an inducement to enter a place of amusement or as an incentive to enter into any business agreement whereby the offer was for the purpose of attracting trade.
(e) Any person who, as the operator of a motor vehicle, strikes a domestic animal shall stop at once and render such assistance as may be possible and shall immediately report such injury or death to the animal's owner; in the event the owner cannot be ascertained and located, such operator shall at once report the accident to the appropriate law enforcement agency or to the local humane society.
(f) No person shall expose any known poisonous substance, whether mixed with food or not, so that the same shall be liable to be eaten by any animal, provided that it shall be lawful for a person to expose on said person's own property common rat poison mixed only with vegetable substance.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-105)
196:
(a) No person shall own, possess, or have custody on said person's premises any wild or vicious animal for display, training, or exhibition purposes, whether gratuitously or for a fee.
(b) No person shall keep, or permit to be kept, any wild animal as a pet.
(c) The licensing authority may order the release of any infant wild animal under temporary permit that is deemed capable of survival.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-107)
197:
(a) No person may sponsor, promote, train a wild animal to participate in, contribute to the involvement of a wild animal in, or attend as a spectator any activity or event in which any wild animal engages in unnatural behavior or is wrestled, fought, mentally or physically harassed, or displayed in such a way that the animal is abused or stressed mentally or physically or is induced or encouraged to perform through the use of chemical, mechanical, electrical, or manual devices in a manner that will cause or is likely to cause physical injury or suffering. This prohibition applies to events and activities taking place in either public or private facilities or property, and applies regardless of the purpose of the events or activities and irrespective to whether or not a fee is charged to spectators.
(b) All equipment used on a performing animal shall fit properly and be in good working condition.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-108)
198:
The owner of every animal shall be responsible for the removal of any excreta deposited by the owner's animals on public walks, recreation areas, or private property.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-109)
199:
The civil and criminal provisions of this article shall be enforced by those persons or agencies designated by municipal authority. It shall be a violation of this article to interfere with a humane officer in the performance of a humane officer's duties.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-110)
200:
Any person violating any provision of this article shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished according to section 1-4. If a violation continues, each day's violation shall be deemed a separate violation. If any person is found guilty by a court of violating section 6-46, said person's permit to own, keep, harbor, or have custody of animals shall be deemed automatically revoked and no new permit may be issued.
(Ord. of 5-2-2005, § 30-111)
205:
All new construction shall meet applicable state minimum standard codes to require the installation of high-efficiency plumbing fixtures.
(Ord. of 9-4-2012, § 1(23.10)(intro. ¶))
206:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Construction means the erection of a new building or the alteration of an existing building in connection with its repair or renovation or in connection with making an addition to an existing building and shall include the replacement of a malfunctioning, unserviceable, or obsolete faucet, showerhead, toilet, or urinal in an existing building.
Department means the department of community affairs.
Lavatory faucet means a faucet that discharges into a lavatory basin in a domestic or commercial installation.
Plumbing fixture means a device that receives water, waste, or both and discharges the water, waste, or both into a drainage system. The term "plumbing fixture" includes a kitchen sink, utility sink, lavatory, bidet, bathtub, shower, urinal, toilet, water closet, or drinking water fountain.
Plumbing fixture fitting means a device that controls and directs the flow of water. The term "plumbing fixture fitting" includes a sink faucet, lavatory faucet, showerhead, or bath filler.
Pressurized flushing device means a device that contains a valve that:
(1) Is attached to a pressurized water supply pipe that is of sufficient size to deliver water at the necessary rate of flow to ensure flushing when the valve is open; and
(2) Opens on actuation to allow water to flow into the fixture at a rate and in a quantity necessary for the operation of the fixture and gradually closes to avoid water hammer.
Toilet means a water closet.
Water closet means a fixture with a water-containing receptor that receives liquid and solid body waste and on actuation conveys the waste through an exposed integral trap into a drainage system and which is also referred to as a toilet.
WaterSenseTM means a voluntary program of the United States Environmental Protection Agency designed to identify and promote water-efficient products and practices.
(Ord. of 9-4-2012, § 1(23.10)(a))
208:
To the extent that the standards set forth in this article exceed the National Energy Conservation Policy Act, as amended, and 10 CFR 430.32, the department is directed to petition the Department of Energy for a waiver of federal preemption pursuant to 42 USC 6297(d).
(Ord. of 9-4-2012, § 1(23.10)(c))
210:
Any person who installs any toilet, faucet, urinal, or shower head in violation of this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Ord. of 9-4-2012, § 1(23.10)(f))
214:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accessories means antennae, lightning rods, whip antennae or other similar projections from the tower.
Construction includes the replacement of existing facilities but does not include any maintenance, repair, or alteration of equipment within an existing structure.
Telecommunications company, transmission facility, andtelecommunications utility are meant to be synonymous, and may hereafter be called subject company, and shall include television, AM radio, FM radio, microwave, cellular telephone, cellular radio, and personal communication systems.
Telecommunications transmission facility, structure, or tower means a facility, structure, or tower built to house and support one or more antennae for transmitting and/or receiving electronic data, radio, television, or telephone communications. The term "antennae" or "antenna array" means a structure attached to a telecommunications structure or tower that supports or is the antenna system for receiving and/or transmitting electronic data, microwave, telephone communications, radio, cellular, or television communications.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 1)
215:
Structures and towers shall be located on the property so that the horizontal distance from the base of the tower in the case of a guyed tower (a tower supported by steel wires) and from any of the anchor points in the case of a lattice-type tower (a tower constructed of crossed structural-steel members) to the adjoining property line under another ownership, to public property, or to the right-of-way of public streets is a minimum of 100 percent of the proposed tower's height, including antennae and other accessories. No variance shall be granted from this minimum setback requirement. All guys and guy anchors shall be set back from the property line to ensure they cannot be reached from an adjoining property and to lessen vandalism.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 2)
216:
No additions, changes or modifications shall be made to a facility or tower unless the addition, change or modification is in conformity with the requirements of this article and an approved authorization to construct.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 3)
217:
Distances in this article shall be measured along a single straight line from each of the anchor points of the tower base in the case of a lattice-type tower (constructed of crossed structural-steel members) and from the tower base itself in the case of a pole-type guyed tower (tower supported by steel cables) to the nearest point on any property line under another ownership or to the right-of-way of any public street.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 4)
218:
(a) Existing vegetation; adverse visual impact. All telecommunications company/utility structures and towers shall be located and sited so as to have the least possible adverse visual impacts on other lands within the city. Existing vegetation shall be preserved to the maximum extent possible to minimize any adverse visual impact on adjoining properties.
(b) Tower illumination. No towers or structures shall be artificially lighted except as required by the city council, or by any state or federal agency such as the Federal Aviation Administration.
(c) Tower finish. For towers not regulated by the Federal Aviation Administration or any state or local aeronautics division, they shall be constructed of such materials and a finish (paint/surface) must be provided that reduces the visibility of the structure from nearby residences and businesses.
(d) Fencing. Security fencing shall be required around the base and around the guy anchors of any tower to minimize vandalism and to minimize exposure to equipment and to the tower, and to minimize exposure of the general public to emissions from these sources that may adversely affect human safety, health, and welfare. A perimeter fence around the property at least six feet in height shall be the preferred method to comply with this section.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 5)
219:
The use of a particular site shall take into account the availability of other locations less likely to cause injury to the neighborhood and their comparative advantages and disadvantages with the property for which approval is sought.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 6)
220:
A subject company requesting permission to share the use of an existing telecommunications company's/utility's structure or tower or parcel of property within the city shall be required to provide documentary evidence of consent from the existing owner, and that such intensified use will not have a detrimental effect on the public health, safety, or welfare, or on other transmission service already being provided.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 7)
221:
(a) The tower shall be erected and operated in compliance with current Federal Communications Commission and other applicable federal, state and local laws, ordinances and regulations.
(b) Subject companies shall notify the city within ten days of the filing of any requests for modification of licenses, permits, or authorizations from any local, state, or federal agency, including the Federal Communications Commission. The subject companies shall also notify the city prior to any change, addition, or modification to the facility or tower, or lease of space or lease or sale of the tower itself, which may subject the residents and the environment of the city to potential adverse health, safety, or welfare effects.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 8)
222:
A telecommunications company or telecommunications utility must file for authority to construct by application. All applications for authority to construct shall contain the information described in exhibit A to the ordinance from which this article is derived.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 9)
223:
At the first council meeting after the expiration of 21 days after the filing of the application, the council shall review it and notify the subject company in writing of any deficiencies in the submitted information and data. The subject company shall correct any deficiencies within 30 days thereafter or explain in writing to the council why it is unable to do so. Any such explanation shall include an estimate of when the subject company will be able to correct the information deficiencies. Upon correction of any deficiencies in the application, any public hearings which are necessary may be held on the application. The council shall issue a decision no later than 120 days after the acceptance of the application as completed or at such later time as is mutually agreed between the subject company and the council.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 10)
224:
No telecommunications facility, structure, or tower shall be installed, erected, or constructed unless the subject company's application for authority to construct and the plans therefor are approved by the city council after consideration of the intent, purposes and standards set forth in this article.
(1) Submission of plans; review.
a. All applications for authority to construct a telecommunications facility, structure, or tower shall be submitted to the city council by delivery to the city clerk at city hall, at least 21 working days prior to the next regularly scheduled city council meeting. The city staff shall review the plans according to the purposes and review criteria set out in this article and make recommendations to the city council.
b. Recommendations of the city staff and a copy of the plans shall be forwarded to the mayor and each member of the city council for review. The city council shall review the plans according to the purposes and review criteria set forth in this article. Upon approval by the city council of the subject company's application for authority to construct, the subject company may apply for a building permit. The subject company must comply with all other applicable ordinances of the city or building codes or flood control, etc.
(2) Contents of application for authority to construct. See exhibit A to the ordinance from which this article is derived for information to be included in an application for authority to construct.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 11)
225:
Within five days after the receipt of a subject company's application for authority to construct, the city clerk shall mail a copy thereof to the Regional Development Center for comment, which comments are due at the next regular council meeting after the initial filing by the subject company.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 12)
226:
(a) On the date the subject company files an application for authority to construct with the city clerk at the city hall, the subject company shall serve a notice by mail on all owners and lessees of property under another ownership adjacent and abutting the proposed site of subject company, to the owner of the proposed site, and to other parties having requested such notification.
(b) No later than five days after such date the company files an application for authority to construct with the city clerk, the subject company shall post a notice as follows:
(1) At three public places in the area: one on each public street adjacent or abutting the proposed site; one in a prominent place at city hall; one in the county newspaper (non-legal section) for a minimum of two weeks. The notices posted near the property shall be of a sufficient size to be read by passing motorists. A declaration of mailing and publishing shall be filed with the council no later than five days after the notice is mailed or published.
(2) Said notice shall include, at a minimum, the following information:
a. A general description of the proposed construction and its location;
b. Instructions on obtaining or reviewing a copy of the application for authority to construct;
c. The applicable procedure for protesting the application permit; and
d. The date the protest period expires.
(c) The city clerk shall send a copy of the application for authority to construct to the mayor and to each councilmember within 24 hours of the city clerk's receipt of same and shall send or deliver a copy to the city's public works engineer.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 13)
227:
(a) Any person may file a protest to the application for a permit. The protest with reasons therefor shall be filed with the city council no later than 30 days after the date on which the application for authority to construct was filed with the city clerk or no later than 30 days after the date the copy of the application for authority to construct was mailed to the protestor or no later than 30 days after the last date said notice was published in the chosen legal organ of the county, whichever date is later. The person protesting shall serve a copy of the protest on the subject company by mail or in person on the same day the protest is filed with the city council.
(b) A protest may be made by letter, telegram, or telefax, or orally at any regular or special meeting of the city council. An oral protest must be transferred to a written protest and filed with the city clerk within two business days after the meeting.
(c) The subject company shall respond in writing to a protest within ten business days after its receipt and shall serve copies of its response by mail on each protestant and the mayor and each member of the council.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 14)
228:
Those to whom notice has been given or sent as specified in this article and any other person entitled to participate in a proceeding for an authority to construct may, within 30 days after the notice was mailed and published, request that the council hold hearings on the application. Any such request should include the reasons therefor. If the council, as a result of its preliminary investigation after such request, determines that public hearings should be held, notice of the date and time of the hearing shall be sent to each person who is entitled to notice and who has requested a hearing, and a public hearing shall be scheduled. A public hearing shall be advertised in the chosen legal organ of the county for a minimum of two weeks immediately prior to a hearing and shall be posted at city hall.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 15)
229:
(a) If no protest has been filed and a public hearing is not held and if it is determined that an environmental impact report is not required, the city council shall review the application for authority to construct at the first regularly scheduled council meeting after the protest period has expired and shall issue a resolution to approve or deny the application for authority to construct.
(b) If a protest has been filed (and an environmental impact report is not required to be filed), the city council shall issue a resolution approving the application for authority to construct or shall reject the application for authority to construct at the first regularly scheduled council meeting after the public hearing.
(c) If an environmental impact report has been filed, the city council shall issue a resolution approving the application for authority to construct or shall deny the application for authority to construct within 60 days after receipt of the report, provided any required public hearings have been held. The additional time is to allow the council to review the environmental impact report.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 16)
231:
Once the city council issues a decision authorizing the proposed construction, the subject company may apply for a building permit and, if all other ordinances are complied with, may commence construction.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 18)
232:
(a) Towers shall be inspected annually by a qualified engineer retained by the subject company or other qualified person. At a minimum, the inspection should cover:
(1) Tower structure, including loose bolts, loose or damaged members, signs of unusual stress or vibration.
(2) Tower vertical alignment.
(3) Guy wire tension: both required tension and present tension.
(4) Guy wires and fittings: check for secureness, rust and vibration.
(5) Guy anchors and foundations: assess for cracks in concrete, signs of corrosion or movement, secure hardware, proper fencing.

(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 19)
233:
Any tower that is no longer used for its original purpose for a period of one year or more shall be removed by the owner at the owner's expense.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 20)
234:
The standards in this article and the requirements will be reviewed by the city periodically to determine their adequacy relative to public safety, health and welfare.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 21)
235:
The owner of a telecommunications facility, structure, or tower shall assume complete liability for any occurrence in connection with the placement or operation of such facility, structure, or tower.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 22)
237:
(a) The following uses are exempt from approval: portable, handheld and vehicular transmissions; marketed consumer products like citizen band radios.
(b) Towers erected by a public agency exclusively for public emergency dispatch systems like 911, EMS, police, fire, sheriff, civil defense, and two-way communication transmitters used by 911, emergency services including fire, police, sheriff, ambulance service, or emergency aid may be exempt from the requirements of this article by an order of the city council after consideration of their request for exemption from this article.
(Ord. of 10-3-1994, § 24)
242:
The purpose of this article is to regulate certain types of businesses to the end that the many types of criminal activities frequently engendered by such businesses and the adverse effect on property values and on the public health, safety, and welfare of the city, and on its citizens and property, and on the character of its neighborhoods and development will be curtailed. This article is not intended to allow or license any business, establishment, or activity which would otherwise be unlawful.
(Ord. of 4-7-1997, § 1)
243:

b. Any business or establishment to which the public or any portion thereof is permitted where employees or patrons expose specified anatomical areas or engage in specified sexual activities; or
c. Any other business or establishment to which the public or any portion thereof is permitted which offers its patrons services or entertainment characterized by an emphasis on matter depicting, describing, discussing or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.

Church means a place where persons regularly assemble for religious worship.
Conviction means adjudication of guilty, plea of guilty, plea of nolo contendere or the forfeiture of a bond when charged with a crime, but shall not include a discharge under provisions of what is commonly called the State of Georgia First Offender Act.
Discharge and measurement means the measurement in lineal feet from the center of any door of customer entry of the proposed premises of an adult entertainment establishment (or if not on ground level, then the beginning point for measuring the distance shall be the point of ground level determined by measuring from the center of any door of customer entry perpendicular to the ground level) to the nearest property line of any church, library, school, college, public park, residence, or hospital. Minor means any person who has not attained the age of 18 years.

Residence means a house, apartment, mobile home, boardinghouse or roominghouse, duplex, or other multifamily housing, for human dwelling, or any properties owned therefor.

(3) Use of human or animal ejaculation, sodomy, oral copulation, coitus, or masturbation;

(5) Sexually oriented torture; or
(6) Fondling or other sexual contact with an animal so as to arouse or excite the sexual desires of a partner.
(Ord. of 4-7-1997, § 2)
244:
The following regulations apply to all adult entertainment establishments as described herein and located within the city:
(1) It shall be unlawful for a licensee to employ, admit or permit the admission of minors within a licensed premises.
(2) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, barter or give to any minor any service, material, device or thing sold or offered for sale by an adult entertainment establishment.

(a) Suspension. The mayor and council may suspend a license for a period of 180 days if the mayor and council determine that the licensee or an employee has violated any section of this article. If the mayor and council deem a license suspension appropriate, they shall so notify the licensee of such decision in writing and the basis thereof. Such suspension shall take effect ten days following the licensee's notification thereof unless an appeal is filed with and to the mayor and council by the aggrieved party on or before ten days of the date of receipt by the aggrieved party of the decision. A hearing by the mayor and council of the appeal shall occur within 30 days of its filing in a regular or special meeting of the mayor and council. Enforcement of the suspension shall be stayed pending the mayor and council's ruling on the licensee's appeal.
(b) Revocation.
(1) The mayor and council may revoke a license if a cause for suspension occurs and the license has been suspended within the past 12 months.
(2) The mayor and council may also revoke a license if they determine that:
a. A licensee gave false or misleading information in the material submitted during the application process.
b. A licensee or an employee knowingly operated the sexually oriented business during a period of time when the license was suspended.
c. A licensee or an employee has knowingly allowed any act of sexual intercourse, sodomy, or copulation, masturbation, or other illegal sexual conduct to occur in or on the licensed premises.
d. The owner or operator of the licensed establishment knowingly allowed a person under 18 years of age to enter the establishment.
(3) If the mayor and council deems a license revocation appropriate, they shall so notify the licensee of such decision in writing and the basis thereof. Such revocation shall take effect ten days following the mayor and council's serving of the written decision upon the licensee unless an appeal is filed with and to the mayor and council by the aggrieved party on or before ten days of the date of receipt by the aggrieved party of the decision of the mayor and council. A hearing by the mayor and council on the decision shall occur within 30 days of its filing in a regular or special meeting of the mayor and council. Revocation shall continue for a one-year period from the date revocation becomes effective.
(c) Appeal procedure. An applicant or licensee who has timely filed an appeal with the mayor and council as allowed by this article shall be entitled to a hearing before the mayor and council. At the time set for the hearing, the mayor and council shall receive all relevant testimony in evidence from city staff or interested parties, and from the licensee or employee. In all hearings pursuant to this article, the following procedures shall apply:
(1) The mayor and council shall read or cause to be read the charges and specifications against the charged party. The mayor and council shall then read or cause to be read any response filed by the charged party.
(2) The mayor and council shall hear the evidence upon the charges and specifications as filed against the charged party and shall not consider any additional evidence beyond the scope of the charges and may exclude evidence which is purely cumulative.
(3) The order of proof shall be as follows: The city representative shall present evidence in support of the charges; the charged party shall then present evidence. Evidence of each party may be supported by submission of pertinent documents. Each party shall be allowed to present pertinent rebuttal evidence.
(4) The charged party and city may be represented by counsel, and may present, examine and cross examine witnesses. Additionally, the mayor and council may interrogate all parties and witnesses to obtain necessary information.
(d) Enforcement action.
(1) Any person violating the provisions of this article shall be punished according to section 1-4.
(2) Should any license be revoked or suspended, all signs indicating that such businesses conducted on the premises shall be removed from the premises during the period of revocation or suspension.
(3) The violation of provisions of this article by any person may be enjoined by instituting appropriate proceedings for injunction in any court of competent jurisdiction. Such action may be maintained notwithstanding that other adequate remedies at law exist.
(e) Service of notice.
(1) Any notice required to be given under this article to any applicant, licensee or employee may be given either by personal delivery or by certified United States mail, postage prepaid, return receipt requested, addressed to the most recent address as specified in the application for license/permit, or such updated address which may have subsequently been provided in writing to the city clerk. Notices mailed as described above shall be deemed given on the second day subsequent to their deposit in the United States mail.
(2) It shall be the duty of each applicant, licensee and employee to furnish notice to the city clerk in writing of any change of mailing address.
(Ord. of 4-7-1997, § 17)

276:
The county sheriff, the deputies thereof, constables, and all other law enforcement officers shall be authorized to issue citations to violators of any provision of this article, as amended. Such citations shall state the time and place at which the accused is to appear for trial, shall identify the offense with which the accused is charged, shall have an identifying number by which it shall be filed with the municipal court, shall indicate the identity of the accused and the date of the service, and shall be signed by the officer who completes and serves it.
(Ord. of 1-5-2016, § 1(1-12))
277:
(a) Any person violating this article, as amended or any provision hereof, upon conviction, shall be punished according to section 1-4 as follows: by a fine of not more than $1,000.00 or imprisonment in the county jail for up to 60 days, or both.
(b) No person accused of violating this article shall be arrested prior to trial, but any person who fails to appear for trial shall be arrested thereafter on the warrant of the municipal court and required to post a bond for the person's future appearance.
(Ord. of 1-5-2016, § 1(1-13))
278:
(a) Violations of this article shall be tried upon citation as described in section 10-92 and may be tried with or without a prosecuting attorney as well as upon accusations. The county attorney shall serve as prosecuting attorney.
(b) Violations of this article shall be tried in the municipal court, and shall be tried in accordance with O.C.G.A. ch. 15-10.
(Ord. of 1-5-2016, § 1(1-14))
281:
There is hereby levied an annual license fee upon each insurer doing business within the city in an amount as established by the city council from time to time. For each separate business location in excess of one not covered by section 10-118, which is operating on behalf of such insurers within the city, there is hereby levied a license fee in an amount as established by the city council from time to time. For the purposes of this article, the term "insurer" means a company which is authorized to transact business in any of the classes of insurance designated in O.C.G.A. § 33-3-5.
(Ord. of 1-9-2012, § 1)
282:
For each separate business location not otherwise subject to a license fee hereunder, operated and maintained by a business organization which is engaged in the business of lending money or transacting sales involving term financing and in connection with such loans or sales offers, solicits or takes application for insurance through a licensed agent of an insurer for insurance, said insurer shall pay an additional license fee in an amount as established by the city council from time to time per location for each year.
(Ord. of 1-9-2012, § 2)
283:
There is hereby levied an annual tax based solely upon gross direct premiums upon each insurer writing life, accident and sickness insurance within the state in an amount equal to one percent of the gross direct premiums received during the preceding calendar year in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.1.
